instruction: Identify each deposit and classify it as salary, service income, current transfer or another lawful current-account category; do not mix business, gift or capital funds into this route.
Collect the valid ID, amount-bearing source-of-funds documents and the tax voucher, exemption certificate or 税务备案表 required for a single payment above USD 50,000.

Ask the bank to confirm in writing that it accepts the documents, the purchase purpose matches the remittance purpose, and the account is classified as 境外个人; get the dated executable rate and itemised fee quote.

Complete the international wire form with the verified payee account/SWIFT details, pay the CNY principal and fees, sign the application, and retain the rate confirmation, tax evidence and wire receipt.
Obtain the bank's written 境内个人 classification and confirm the genuine current-account purpose.
Complete the 个人购汇申请书 and assemble amount-bearing purpose documents; above USD 50,000/day also assemble outward-remittance transaction materials.
Check purchase/remittance purpose consistency with the bank and obtain the dated rate and fee quote; do not split the application across people.
Sign the wire application, pay principal and fees, and retain the application, quote, tax recordal if applicable and receipt.
Obtain a currency-by-currency statement showing the balance is already USD/FX rather than CNY.
Confirm the bank's 境外个人/境内个人 classification and whether the USD 50,000/day documentation threshold applies.
Request the written wire/cable quote and verified receiving-bank/SWIFT details; no FX purchase means no bid/ask spread.
Sign the wire application, pay the wire/cable fees and retain the receipt; review U.S. §988 and reporting separately.
Locate the original 兑换水单 and confirm its exchange date is within 24 months.
Ask the bank to confirm the unused amount shown by the slip and that no income/tax documents are needed for this reconversion.
Obtain the dated rate and wire/cable quote and the receiving-bank instructions.
Sign the wire application, pay principal and fees, and retain the slip, quote and receipt.
Confirm the amount is within the official ID-only daily limit (≤USD 500/day; ≤USD 1,000/day at border-side outlets).
Present valid ID at the bank/authorised outlet and ask for the written banknote rate and fee before transacting.
If carrying cash, observe the PRC cash-export permit and U.S. Form 105 declaration rules; do not exceed them.
Stop: this rule cannot execute USD 10,000-400,000 as one transaction; use a documented route or obtain the original slip.
Confirm you actually hold the PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card; a U.S. passport alone does not qualify for purchase on ID alone.
Confirm the remaining USD 50,000 equivalent convenience amount for the calendar year with the bank in writing.
Obtain the dated rate and per-wire fee quote, then repeat one compliant wire per calendar year for each full USD 50,000 tranche plus the remainder.
Retain each year's application, quote and receipt; do not borrow anyone else's quota.
Complete the property title transfer and obtain the registered transfer contract and title-transfer proof.
Obtain the tax voucher and, for a single payment above USD 50,000, the applicable 税务备案表; compute the 20% IIT on gain using original cost and reasonable expenses.
Ask the bank to confirm the remittance ceiling (transfer price minus taxes/fees and ownership share) and obtain the dated rate and wire quote.
Sign the wire application and retain the property, tax, approval and wire records for PRC and U.S. credit/reporting purposes.
Gather inheritance proof, property documents and the tax certificate for the estate; confirm the decedent's last hukou location.
File the 继承转移 application with the SAFE office at that hukou location and obtain the written approval amount.
Give the bank the approval, your own overseas account details and tax certificate; ask whether it will remit once or in instalments and obtain the rate/fee quote.
Retain every approval and wire record; report a foreign bequest above USD 100,000 on Form 3520 and review U.S. tax treatment.
Gather hukou-cancellation proof, certified settlement proof, property/source documents and tax certificates; confirm the former hukou location.
File the 移民转移 application with the SAFE office at the former hukou location and obtain the written approval amount.
Give the bank the approval and own overseas account details; ask for the one-or-instalment remittance schedule and dated rate/fee quote.
Retain approvals, tax certificates and wire receipts; complete U.S. reporting and §988 review.
Confirm the money is genuine distributable corporate profit, not personal savings, and obtain the board/partnership resolution and accounts.
Obtain the tax filing form for a payment above USD 50,000 and decide, with evidence, whether the 10% treaty position is supportable; otherwise use the 20% statutory IIT.
Ask the bank for the written tax/document review, dated rate and wire quote; do not disguise personal funds as a dividend.
Sign the wire application and retain resolution, tax recordal, treaty evidence, quote and receipt for Form 1116/U.S. reporting.
Confirm with the sending bank in writing that it offers personal outbound RMB for this exact genuine current-account transaction.
Collect the same authenticity and tax documents required for the underlying transaction; obtain the receiving bank's CNY account instructions.
Request written sending-bank fees and the offshore bank's CNY→USD conversion rate/fee; do not proceed until the all-in USD received is known.
Only then authorise the RMB wire; retain both banks' quotes and receipts and complete U.S. §988/reporting review.
Confirm the card is a mainland UnionPay debit card on the RMB account and read BOC's current card fee.
Check the RMB 10,000/card/day and RMB 100,000/person/calendar-year caps before choosing amounts.
Obtain UnionPay's dated conversion rate and the foreign ATM owner's on-screen fee; leave the all-in cost blank until both are written.
If physically carrying more than USD 10,000 into the U.S., file FinCEN Form 105; retain withdrawal and declaration records.
First lawfully buy the foreign currency through an eligible route and obtain the bank's cash-selling rate and banknote withdrawal fee.
For USD 5,000-10,000 obtain the bank's 携带外汇出境许可证; do not carry more than USD 10,000 without the required SAFE permit.
Before entering the U.S., determine whether the family/group carries more than USD 10,000 and prepare FinCEN Form 105.
Retain the purchase, permit, declaration and banknote records; this is a delivery method, not a way around source/tax rules.
List the accounts to consolidate and confirm each belongs to the same person or a close relative in the same subject category.
Ask the bank in writing whether a 境内个人↔境外个人 FX-account transfer would be treated as cross-border; do not make that transfer casually.
Consolidate the balance, then select one lawful outward route (B01/B02/B04/B07 etc.) and obtain its documents and quote.
Send one outward wire and retain consolidation and wire records.
Confirm there is a real cross-border service with a contract/invoice/settlement list; personal savings do not qualify.
For a single payment above USD 50,000, obtain the tax record-filing form; below the threshold ask the bank what it reviews.
Obtain the dated rate and itemised wire quote and confirm the purpose matches the service documents.
Sign the wire application and retain contract, tax, quote and receipt; never fabricate a trade background.
Confirm a real foreign-invested enterprise termination, completed liquidation and tax payment; personal savings are out of scope.
Obtain the liquidation/tax evidence and any SAFE/bank approvals for the RMB belonging to the foreign investor.
Ask the bank for the dated FX rate and wire quote within the approved amount.
Sign the wire application and retain liquidation, tax, approval and wire records.
Confirm the balance is lawful RMB salary and obtain employment/income and tax evidence.
Ask the sending bank in writing whether it offers personal cross-border RMB salary remittance under 银发〔2018〕3号 and what documents it requires.
Obtain the receiving bank's CNY account instructions and its written CNY→USD rate/fee; the PBOC article does not publish these costs.
Only after both quotes, authorise the RMB wire, retain records, and complete U.S. §988/reporting review.
Stop: no official rule read here permits a foreign passport holder to convert and remit gift or undocumented RMB.
Ask the bank in writing whether any lawful route exists for the exact facts and what document would be required.
If the funds are a foreign gift/bequest, obtain U.S. Form 3520 advice before accepting or moving them.
Do not use quota splitting, private swaps or false documents; choose a documented lawful route or leave the funds in place.
Do not split the purchase across relatives, friends or multiple people.
Ask the bank which documented single-wire route fits the genuine source of funds.
If past splitting occurred, obtain professional advice before any correction filing; the watch-list lasts current year plus two.
Use only the lawful route with complete source/tax documents and retain the written bank decision.
Do not use an app, WeChat contact, broker, underground bank or private offset arrangement.
Verify that the counterparty is a qualified bank, licensed exchange institution or authorised agency.
Ask the licensed institution for the documented route and written quote; do not provide false purpose documents.
Retain the licence verification, source/tax documents and official receipt.
Do not buy crypto, a stablecoin or an RWA token with RMB to move value out of China.
Close any proposed fiat/virtual-currency conversion plan; the 2026 PBOC notice repeals the 2021 notice and prohibits the activity.
Ask a qualified bank for a documented current-account or approval route instead.
Retain the written bank decision and all source/tax documents.
Do not prepare false invoices, a false purchase purpose or false source documents.
Do not carry undeclared currency/monetary instruments above USD 10,000 into/out of the U.S.; prepare FinCEN Form 105 if required.
Ask the bank/tax office for the genuine document list and written decision for the lawful route.
Retain genuine documents, declarations and receipts; never split to avoid review.
FBAR: For each calendar year, compute the aggregate maximum of all foreign accounts; FBAR is required if it exceeded USD 10,000 at any time.
FBAR: File FinCEN Form 114 electronically through the BSA e-filing system by April 15 (automatic extension to October 15).
FBAR: Keep the filing confirmation and account statements; if a year was missed, review IRM 4.26.16.3.11 and streamlined/delinquent options.
Form 8938: Compare the year-end and anytime maxima against the IRS thresholds for filing status and residence.
Form 8938: File Form 8938 with the income tax return when required; FBAR is separate and does not replace it.
Form 8938: If a prior Form 8938 was missed, use the IRS delinquent international information return procedures with a reasonable-cause statement where appropriate.
Form 3520: Identify whether any amount received was a gift/bequest from a nonresident alien/foreign estate exceeding USD 100,000 in the year.
Form 3520: Report it on Form 3520 Part IV and keep donor/estate documents.
Form 3520: If late, review the §6039F 5%/month (max 25%) penalty and reasonable-cause exception with a professional.
26 U.S.C. §988: Reconstruct the date and USD basis of each CNY acquisition; IRS yearly averages are labelled scenarios, not an official spot rate.
26 U.S.C. §988: Determine with a professional whether the disposition is a personal transaction and whether §162/§212 expenses remove personal treatment.
26 U.S.C. §988: Report ordinary gain/loss where applicable; personal gain of USD 200 or less is excluded under §988(e)(2).
Foreign tax credit: Obtain official PRC tax certificates for income tax actually paid on the same income.
Foreign tax credit: Have Form 1116 prepared, applying the foreign tax credit limitations.
Foreign tax credit: Retain the treaty and tax records; the saving clause preserves U.S. taxation of citizens.
Correction procedures: Determine residency, prior filing history, willfulness and whether IRS has contacted you.
Correction procedures: Choose the published path: SFOP, SDOP, delinquent international information returns, delinquent FBARs, or IRS Criminal Investigation voluntary disclosure.
Correction procedures: File the required 3 years of returns and 6 years of FBARs, certifications and reasonable-cause statements with professional review.
